inference: Health status alone is not the trigger: the information must relate to health, care or payment for care AND identify an individual, and it must be held by a listed holder type. Payment for care brings billing records within scope when the payer or provider relationship is health-related.
location: 45 CFR 160.103, definitions of individually identifiable health information and protected health information
statement: Individually identifiable health information is a subset of health information that is created or received by a health care provider, health plan, employer or clearinghouse, relates to the past, present or future health or condition of an individual, the provision of health care to an individual, or the past, present or future payment for that care, and identifies the individual or gives a reasonable basis to believe it can identify the individual. Protected health information is individually identifiable health information that is transmitted or maintained in electronic or other form (with listed exclusions).

notes: Read from a mirror of the regulation, not the eCFR page itself.
The definition's exclusion paragraphs (education records, employment records held as employer) were not worked through; they bear on employer-held and customer-held data.

inference: A value inside a JSON string keeps its bytes when it contains no escaped character; the adjacent backslash-quote pairs are syntax. statement: A JSON string is delimited by quotation marks; quotation mark, reverse solidus and control characters U+0000 to U+001F must be escaped; any character may be escaped, including as a six-character \uXXXX sequence.

notes: Nested JSON (a JSON document inside a string) adds one escape level per nesting; only one level is exercised.

inference: Project inference: a value with prefix letter Q, an excluded prefix or a suffix outside A-D cannot be an issued NINO, and the documented example is therefore safe to publish; it still has the NINO structure, which is why it is a usable positive for structural recognition.

notes: The page lists exclusions as currently stated; HMRC may change allocation rules.
